# Source baseline, progress and resume

Find the plan by argument path/ID or target backend index; multiple matching revisions need a focused question, not selecting the first file. Read foundation/spec/contracts/test matrix/reliability/tasks/DoD, context/ADRs and current implementation. Record plan ID/revision/source commit, contract/schema revision, target-code HEAD and dirty/untracked changes. Source plan-ready does not mean foundations are implemented: task prerequisites may require bootstrap before the feature.

For blocking unresolved foundation/contract choices return dependent work to planning clarification; continue independent ready tasks. A new build does not authorize simplifying stack/business/SLA thresholds. Spec changes are proposed/accepted on actual grounds with new revision/impact maps and updated tasks/tests/DoD. Do not pretend an old revision was implemented without deviations.

Initialize or read canonical ledger/source-plan section under [progress](../progress.md). For old plans without markers add a dedicated execution section preserving semantics; for missing ledgers inventory all source TASK IDs, not only convenient ones. Run helpers on source ledgers outside plugin caches. Without source-plan write access report the synchronization blocker and save a safe local report; never claim the plan was updated.

Before rerunning, check evidence against actual code: prior-agent messages/old PASS remain claims until commits/artifacts/scope are verified. Never overwrite others' dirty changes or claim them as your implemented commits. With unrelated work choose a suitable isolated integration checkout per project policy; explicitly include in-scope dirty edits in frozen bases or careful scoped patches without loss or unrelated commits.

At every event update ledger and **the plan itself**: dispatch→in_progress, code handoff→implemented, integration acceptance→integrated, actual checks→verified, issues→blocked or regression states. Preserve task/plan revision/evidence/commit and reasons for remaining work. Only the coordinator writes shared progress/index; child agents return task reports from their worktrees.
